subject: determine whether a neighbourhood value is significantly different from the city value

messages.author: 33c8aec318ed172d
messages.subject: determine whether a neighbourhood value is significantly different from the city value
parts:
Hi everyone,

I have a dataset with all neighbourhoods in a city and a value for each neighbourhood (a rate). I would like to be able to create an interactive vizualization that enables the user to select individual neighbourhoods and find out whether the value of that neighbourhood is significantly higher or lower than the city average across all neighbourhoods (I have a value that was calculated for the city). Given that the neighbourhoods are contiguous areas composing the city, there is spatial dependency, so I cannot use z scores or apply other classical statistics test since the observations are not independent and spatial autocorrelation might exist. Therefore, I need to ensure the code I use to create this interactive vizualization accounts for spatial dependency.

I recently received some great advice, to look into R-INLA, to employ a BYM model and to calculate a linear combination of the iid and besag part of the BYM model for each neighbourhood. 

I was wondering if this looks like a good approach. I tried to adapt the Germany code, but I am not sure how to deal with the linear combinations:

data(city)
g = system.file("/city.graph", package="INLA")
summary(city)

## just make a duplicated column
city = cbind(g,region.struct=city$neighbourhood)

# standard BYM model (without covariates)
formula1 = Y ~ f(region.struct,model="besag",graph.file=g) +
               f(region,model="iid")


result1  =  inla(formula1,family="gaussian",data=city)


I am not sure how to use the  'inla.make.lincombs()' function to test whether the value for each neighbourhood is statistically different from the city value. Any help is very much appreciated!

Thank you very much!

Dani
